# Results — Study 949 (Riding the TIPS Curve) on the real daily tape

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). Two questions. **(1)** Does
extending along the **real** yield curve pay? — race the four inflation-linked maturity
buckets **excess-of-cash** (minus BIL's actual total return). **(2)** Is what survives a
duration hedge a real carry? — regress each linker's excess return on a
**duration-matched nominal Treasury fund's** excess return, with the hedge beta fitted on
the trailing 252 days **through day t−1 and applied at day t** (the study's one and only
execution lag), and put a Newey-West *t* on the residual. Daily **total-return** closes
(`yfinance`, `auto_adjust=True`) — never price-only, since a linker's inflation accrual
is paid out as distributions. Common window 2012-10-16 → 2026-06-30 (VTIP's inception
gates it). As-of **2026-06-30**; the partial current month is dropped.*

## Data stamp

| Legs | Window | n days | Fingerprint |
|---|---|---|---|
| VTIP, SCHP, TIP, LTPZ (linkers); SHY, IEF, TLT (nominal matches); BIL (cash) | 2012-10-16 → 2026-06-30 | 3,444 | Fingerprint `9da861d9d566` |

IEI is cached as a robustness pairing. The cash leg (BIL) compounded at **+1.59%/yr**
over this window — a sample that contains both the zero-rate decade and the 2023-2026
5% regime, so the excess-of-cash race is measured against the real path of short rates,
not a flat proxy.

**Assumptions and proxies, named up front.** (i) The linker↔nominal *pairing* comes from
the sponsors' published durations, not from the tape — swept in §7. (ii) The short leg's
**borrow fee is a proxy**, base case 30 bps/yr, swept 0→100 in §6. (iii) One-way cost
2 bps, swept 0→10. (iv) BIL stands in for cash. **Survivorship:** none in the usual sense
— the four buckets are named live ETFs chosen ex ante by maturity, and no fund in the set
was delisted; what *is* a selection effect is the **inception gate** (VTIP launched
2012-10, LTPZ 2009-09), which confines the whole study to the post-GFC real-rate regime.
(v) **Multiplicity, named up front too:** the headline sleeve VTIP−SHY is the *best of
four*, identified after the analysis, and this study computes **56** HAC *t*s on the real
tape in total. §8 ranks every one of them; a Bonferroni bar on 56 tests is |*t*| ≈ 3.2,
and the largest number anywhere is +2.04 — so no adjustment is needed to reach the null,
only honesty about which numbers were looked at.

## 1. The ladder, excess-of-cash

Buy-and-hold funds; no timing, no turnover, no costs to charge (the expense ratio is
already inside the NAV). Drawdowns are shown both excess-of-cash and absolute (lived).

| Bucket | Real duration | Excess return | Vol | Excess Sharpe | HAC *t* | Excess DD | Abs CAGR | Abs DD |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **VTIP** | ~2.5y | **+0.65%** | 2.54% | **+0.256** | +0.99 | −7.4% | +2.23% | −6.3% |
| **SCHP** | ~7y | +0.35% | 5.48% | +0.064 | +0.24 | −18.4% | +1.80% | −14.3% |
| **TIP** | ~7y | +0.27% | 5.61% | +0.049 | +0.19 | −18.7% | +1.71% | −14.5% |
| **LTPZ** | ~20y | **−0.02%** | 14.68% | **−0.001** | −0.00 | −44.8% | +0.49% | −41.0% |

Extending along the real curve did not pay — it paid **less**, monotonically:

| Difference | Per year | HAC *t* | Sharpe gap |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| SCHP − VTIP | −0.30% | −0.32 | −0.192 |
| TIP − VTIP | −0.38% | −0.39 | −0.207 |
| LTPZ − VTIP | −0.67% | −0.21 | −0.257 |

None of the differences is significant — the honest statement is not "long linkers lose"
but **"nothing in this ladder is distinguishable from zero"**. The bootstrap agrees:

| Bucket | Excess Sharpe | 95% CI (2,000 draws, 21-day blocks) | share < 0 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| VTIP | +0.256 | [−0.193, +0.767] | 13.6% |
| SCHP | +0.064 | [−0.409, +0.575] | 38.8% |
| TIP | +0.049 | [−0.417, +0.545] | 41.8% |
| LTPZ | −0.001 | [−0.462, +0.454] | 49.8% |

Thirteen and a half years of holding long TIPS delivered **+0.49%/yr absolute**, below
the **+1.59%/yr** the T-bill leg paid for doing nothing, in exchange for a **−41%**
drawdown. That is the headline fact of this tape: real duration was uncompensated.

## 2. The duration-hedged residual carry

Long the linker, short `beta_{t−1}` of the nominal match. Net charges 2 bps one-way on
|Δbeta| × NAV and 30 bps/yr borrow on |beta| × NAV (the long leg is buy-and-hold and pays
nothing).

| Sleeve | Mean beta | Gross carry | HAC *t* | Net carry | HAC *t* | Net Sharpe | Vol | Turnover |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **VTIP − SHY** | 1.12 | **+0.98%/yr** | **+1.55** | **+0.60%/yr** | **+0.94** | +0.277 | 2.16% | 2.3×/yr |
| SCHP − IEF | 0.68 | +0.69%/yr | +0.68 | +0.47%/yr | +0.47 | +0.141 | 3.35% | 0.6×/yr |
| TIP − IEF | 0.69 | +0.55%/yr | +0.54 | +0.33%/yr | +0.33 | +0.096 | 3.49% | 0.6×/yr |
| LTPZ − TLT | 0.86 | +0.34%/yr | +0.15 | +0.07%/yr | +0.03 | +0.009 | 8.22% | 0.6×/yr |

The residual is **positive in every bucket and significant in none**; the largest
full-sample *t* in the study is **+1.55**, well short of the |*t*| ≥ 2 bar. (The single
number in the whole study that does clear 2 is +2.04 — the *gross* carry of this same
sleeve inside the hand-picked 2021-2023 shock window; see §3 and the full ranking in §8.)
And it *shrinks* with duration —
the exact opposite of what a roll-down story predicts if the real curve's slope is what
you are being paid for. Bootstrapping the headline sleeve:

| VTIP − SHY | Point | 95% CI | share < 0 |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| Gross | +0.98%/yr | [−0.27%, +2.11%] | 5.8% |
| Net | +0.60%/yr | [−0.66%, +1.73%] | 15.9% |

For reference only, the **in-sample** full-sample OLS alphas (hedge fitted on the whole
history, so not tradable) tell the same story with the same term structure:
VTIP~SHY +0.86%/yr (*t* = +1.47, β 1.016, R² 0.317); SCHP~IEF +0.46% (*t* = +0.48,
R² 0.637); TIP~IEF +0.38% (*t* = +0.39); LTPZ~TLT +0.24% (*t* = +0.11, R² 0.699).

## 3. Era cut — the 2021-2023 inflation shock (gross **and** net)

The "pre-shock" era starts at the **sleeve's first day, 2013-10-21**, not 2013-01-01: the
252-day beta warmup eats the first year. It is **1,813 trading days ≈ 7.2 years**, not
eight — the earlier phrasing of this table overstated it, and it is corrected here.

| Sleeve | pre-shock 2013-10-21 → 2020-12-31 (1,813d) | shock 2021-2023 (753d) | post-shock 2024+ (625d) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| **VTIP − SHY** gross | **+0.18%** (*t* = +0.19) | **+2.81%** (***t* = +2.04**) | +1.09% (*t* = +1.45) |
| **VTIP − SHY** net | **−0.20%** (*t* = −0.22) | **+2.36%** (*t* = +1.72) | +0.79% (*t* = +1.05) |
| SCHP − IEF gross | +0.31% (*t* = +0.22) | +1.75% (*t* = +0.74) | +0.50% (*t* = +0.44) |
| SCHP − IEF net | +0.09% (*t* = +0.06) | +1.54% (*t* = +0.65) | +0.29% (*t* = +0.26) |
| TIP − IEF gross | +0.17% (*t* = +0.12) | +1.60% (*t* = +0.68) | +0.39% (*t* = +0.35) |
| TIP − IEF net | −0.05% (*t* = −0.04) | +1.39% (*t* = +0.59) | +0.19% (*t* = +0.17) |
| LTPZ − TLT gross | +0.42% (*t* = +0.13) | +0.44% (*t* = +0.08) | −0.02% (*t* = −0.01) |
| LTPZ − TLT net | +0.15% (*t* = +0.05) | +0.18% (*t* = +0.03) | −0.28% (*t* = −0.12) |

Seven-plus pre-shock years produced **nothing** — gross +0.18%/yr at *t* = +0.19, and the
net sleeve is slightly negative. Everything the study found lives in and after the
inflation shock. That is the decisive diagnostic, because a long-linker / short-nominal
residual is by construction a **long-breakeven** position: it earns realised inflation
minus the breakeven priced at entry. When realised inflation blows past what was priced —
2021-2023 — that leg pays, and no amount of roll-down is needed to explain it.

**The one number in this study that clears |*t*| ≥ 2 is in this table**, and it is worth
stating plainly rather than burying it: the VTIP−SHY *gross* carry inside the shock window
is **+2.81%/yr at HAC *t* = +2.04**. It is not evidence for roll-down and this desk does
not treat it as such — it is (a) a *sub-window chosen after the fact*, one of 56 statistics
computed here, against a Bonferroni bar of ≈3.2; (b) *gross*, i.e. before the borrow the
permanently-short leg must pay, which drops it to *t* = +1.72; and (c) confined to exactly
the three years the study identifies as the inflation surprise. A roll-down carry that
only exists inside the one CPI shock in the sample is the alternative hypothesis, not the
claim. Full ranking of all 56 *t*s in §8.

## 4. Jackknife — drop 2021

2021's **returns** are excised. The hedge beta is *not* re-estimated without 2021, so
betas in early 2022 still carry a 2021 estimation window — named here because it is the
kind of thing that is easy to leave unsaid.

| Sleeve | Gross ex-2021 | HAC *t* | Net ex-2021 | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| VTIP − SHY | +0.53%/yr | +0.80 | **+0.17%/yr** | **+0.26** |
| SCHP − IEF | +0.02%/yr | +0.02 | −0.19%/yr | −0.19 |
| TIP − IEF | −0.10%/yr | −0.09 | −0.32%/yr | −0.30 |
| LTPZ − TLT | −0.59%/yr | −0.25 | −0.86%/yr | −0.37 |

Removing a **single calendar year** — 2021, when the VTIP−SHY sleeve made **+6.38% gross**
against a full-sample average of +0.98% — takes the whole result with it. Three of the
four sleeves turn negative net.

## 5. Calendar years of the headline sleeve (VTIP − SHY, %)

| 2013¹ | 2014 | 2015 | 2016 | 2017 | 2018 | 2019 | 2020 | **2021** | 2022 | 2023 | 2024 | 2025 | 2026¹ |
|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| −0.47 | −2.36 | −0.54 | +1.54 | +0.55 | −0.86 | +1.53 | +1.79 | **+6.38** | +1.63 | +0.51 | +0.63 | +1.19 | +0.87 |

Gross. ¹**Both 2013 (n = 50 days, beta warmup) and 2026 (n = 123 days, to the as-of cut)
are part years**, so an unweighted average across these rows is a summary statistic, not a
return — the annualised figures in §2-§3 are the ones to quote. With that said: **four of
the eight pre-2021 rows are negative**, none exceeds +1.8%, 2021 alone is four times the
full-sample mean, and the unweighted mean of the pre-2021 rows is +0.15%.

## 6. Friction sweeps (VTIP − SHY)

| One-way cost (borrow 30 bps/yr) | Net carry | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|
| 0 bps (gross of trading) | +0.64%/yr | +1.02 |
| 2 bps (base case) | +0.60%/yr | +0.94 |
| 5 bps | +0.53%/yr | +0.84 |
| 10 bps | +0.42%/yr | +0.66 |

| Borrow (cost 2 bps) | Net carry | HAC *t* | Net Sharpe |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 0 bps/yr (free short — unattainable) | +0.93%/yr | +1.47 | +0.433 |
| 25 bps/yr | +0.65%/yr | +1.03 | +0.303 |
| **30 bps/yr (base case, a PROXY)** | **+0.60%/yr** | **+0.94** | **+0.277** |
| 50 bps/yr | +0.37%/yr | +0.59 | +0.173 |
| 100 bps/yr | **−0.19%/yr** | −0.29 | −0.087 |

Borrow, not trading cost, is what kills it — the sleeve is short every day, so the fee is
a level charge. The whole edge is gone by **~1% borrow**, which is not an exotic rate for a
retail short.

## 7. Pairing and estimation-window robustness

| Sleeve | Mean beta | Gross | HAC *t* | Net | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| VTIP hedged with SHY | 1.12 | +0.98% | +1.55 | +0.60% | +0.94 |
| VTIP hedged with IEI | 0.37 | +0.76% | +1.24 | +0.64% | +1.04 |
| VTIP hedged with IEF | 0.19 | +0.68% | +1.09 | +0.61% | +0.99 |
| SCHP hedged with IEF | 0.68 | +0.69% | +0.68 | +0.47% | +0.47 |
| SCHP hedged with IEI | 1.17 | +0.86% | +0.81 | +0.49% | +0.46 |
| LTPZ hedged with TLT | 0.86 | +0.34% | +0.15 | +0.07% | +0.03 |
| LTPZ hedged with IEF | 1.83 | +0.64% | +0.26 | +0.06% | +0.02 |

The result is *not* a pairing artefact — every alternative match gives the same small,
insignificant positive. Beta window: 126d → +0.28%/yr (*t* = +0.45); 252d → +0.60%
(*t* = +0.94); 504d → **+0.84% (*t* = +1.24)**. Even the most flattering window falls
short — and note that this, not the headline +0.60%/yr, is **the largest net figure
anywhere in the study**; the headline row is the *base-case* specification, not the best
one. Naming the best one and showing that it still fails is the point of the sweep.

## 8. The multiplicity audit — every real-tape *t*, ranked

The headline sleeve VTIP−SHY was picked **after the fact** as the best of four, so this
study owes the reader the full list rather than its own favourite number. It computes
**56** HAC *t*s on the real tape. Ranked by |*t*|, the top of that list is:

| HAC *t* | Statistic |
|--:|---|
| **+2.04** | VTIP−SHY **gross**, sub-window "shock 2021-2023" — **the only one ≥ 2** |
| +1.72 | VTIP−SHY net, sub-window "shock 2021-2023" |
| +1.55 | VTIP−SHY sleeve, gross, 252d beta (**the best full-sample number**) |
| +1.47 | VTIP~SHY full-sample OLS alpha (in-sample hedge) |
| +1.45 | VTIP−SHY gross, sub-window "post-shock 2024+" |
| +1.24 | VTIP−SHY sleeve, net, 504d beta |
| +1.24 | VTIP−IEI sleeve, gross, 252d beta |
| +1.09 | VTIP−IEF sleeve, gross, 252d beta |

**1 of 56 reaches |*t*| ≥ 2**, against a Bonferroni bar of ≈**3.2** for 56 tests — and it
is a gross, post-hoc, three-year sub-window of the best-of-four sleeve, i.e. precisely the
inflation shock this study names as the rival explanation. On the **full sample nothing
exceeds |*t*| = 1.55**. No adjustment is needed to reach the null verdict; what is needed,
and is supplied here, is disclosure of how many numbers were looked at.

## 9. Synthetic control (offline; machinery proof, never supports the stamp)

- **Planted 2.00%/yr residual carry** → recovered **+2.19%/yr, HAC *t* = +3.65** (hedge
  beta 0.83 vs 0.85 planted). The detector finds a carry of the size claimed, easily, on
  a shorter sample than the real one.
- **Null (no carry planted)** → **+0.19%/yr, *t* = +0.32**; across 8 seeds mean *t* =
  +0.50, sd 1.04, fires |*t*| ≥ 2 on **0/8**. The detector does not manufacture carry.
- **Ladder panel** with the *same* carry planted in all three buckets → recovered
  +2.07%, +2.08%, +1.55% — a flat term structure, as it should be. So the real tape's
  *declining* carry term structure is a property of the tape, not of the estimator.

The harness is powered and unbiased: had a ~2%/yr real-yield roll-down carry been there,
this machinery would have stamped it at *t* > 3.

## Verdict

- **Signal — None.** Neither form of the claim survives. **(a)** Extending along the real
  curve paid nothing: excess Sharpe falls monotonically from **+0.256** (VTIP) to
  **−0.001** (LTPZ), every long-minus-short difference is negative and insignificant, and
  every bucket's Sharpe CI straddles zero. **(b)** The duration-hedged residual is
  positive in all four buckets but **significant in none** — the best **full-sample** HAC
  *t* is **+1.55** gross, **+0.94** net, with a bootstrap CI [−0.66%, +1.73%] that includes
  zero. **(c)** What residual exists is one regime: **+0.18%/yr gross (*t* = +0.19), −0.20%
  net, across the 7.2 pre-shock years**, **+2.36%/yr net during 2021-2023**, and dropping
  2021 alone leaves **+0.17%/yr (*t* = +0.26)**. That pattern is the signature of a
  *long-breakeven inflation surprise*, not of a roll-down carry — and the two are not
  separately identifiable from fund returns, which is exactly why the null verdict is the
  honest one. **(d)** Exactly one of the 56 *t*s computed here reaches 2 — **+2.04**, the
  gross carry of the best-of-four sleeve *inside* the shock window (§3, §8). Against a
  Bonferroni bar of ≈3.2, and sitting precisely where the rival hypothesis predicts it, it
  is the alternative explanation showing up on cue, not the claim surviving.
- **Tradability — Mirage.** The best net figure anywhere in the study is **+0.84%/yr**
  (VTIP−SHY on a 504-day beta, *t* = +1.24); the base-case specification pays **+0.60%/yr
  at 2.16% vol**. Either way it comes from a sleeve that is short a Treasury ETF every day:
  it dies at **~1%/yr borrow**, it dies on removing one calendar year, and its whole
  13.5-year history is one inflation shock. Buying it as a *fund* rather than a spread is
  worse still: the long bucket under-earned T-bills by **1.1 pp/yr** while drawing down
  **−41%**.
- **What the tape does say.** The one durable, if unprovable, ordering is that the
  **short** end of the linker curve was the least bad place to sit — VTIP was the only
  bucket to beat cash at all, at a tenth of LTPZ's volatility. That is a statement about
  where the risk was *not* rewarded, not an edge to harvest.
